question: What Windows installer TLS recovery policy should OpenClaw ship when npm fails with leaf-certificate verification errors during `install.ps1`?
rationale: The bug blocks first-time Windows setup, but retrying with `--strict-ssl=false` or silently changing trust roots changes the installer trust boundary and needs maintainer security intent.

options.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
options.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit `cafile` or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

options.title: Operator-approved strict-ssl fallback
options.body: Allow a clearly warned interactive-only `--strict-ssl=false` retry while failing non-interactive installs with remediation instructions.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Keep the installer fail-closed and document npm CA repair, accepting that this setup path remains blocked for affected users.

recommendation.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
recommendation.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit `cafile` or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

likelyOwner.reason: `vincentkoc` has the strongest recent history on the Windows installer path and npm failure handling affected here.
